# 16 — Set Power Series

A set power series is a table $f[S]$ for every subset of an $n$-element
universe.  Think of $f[S]$ as the weight of an object whose label set is
exactly $S$.  This is useful when labels must be distributed without overlap:
vertices of a graph, people in teams, or elements of a partition.  Algebraically
it is

$$R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}]/(x_0^{2},\ldots,x_{n-1}^{2}),$$

so multiplication discards terms that reuse an element.  For example,
$x^{\{0,1\}}x^{\{1,2\}}=0$ because label $1$ was used twice, while
$x^{\{0\}}x^{\{1,2\}}=x^{\{0,1,2\}}$.  This one rule turns partitions into
powers and connected-component extraction into logarithms.

## 1. Subset convolution as multiplication

$$ (f*g)[S]=\sum_{T\subseteq S}f[T]g[S\setminus T]. $$

The formula chooses one submask $T$ for each $S$, so evaluating it directly for
all $S$ costs $O(3^n)$.  The fast algorithm keeps track of cardinality.  Define

$$\widehat f_k[S]=\sum_{T\subseteq S,\ |T|=k}f[T],$$

which is an ordinary subset zeta transform of the layer $|T|=k$.  For each mask,
convolve the short sequences $\widehat f_0[S],\ldots,\widehat f_n[S]$ and
$\widehat g_0[S],\ldots,\widehat g_n[S]$, then Möbius-invert each layer.  The
entry of layer $|S|$ is $(f*g)[S]$: reaching total size $|S|$ forces the two
chosen pieces to be disjoint.  The result costs $O(n^2 2^n)$ time and
$O(n2^n)$ memory.  Unlike OR convolution, the two pieces must be disjoint.

## 2. Functions of a set series

When $g[\varnothing]=0$, every product of more than $n$ copies of $g$ reuses a
label, so $g^{n+1}=0$.  This **nilpotence** makes an apparently infinite formal
series finite.  Substituting $g$ into an exponential generating series
$F(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}F_kz^k/k!$ gives

$$F(g)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}F_k\frac{g^{k}}{k!}.$$

Here $g^k$ first chooses an **ordered** list of $k$ disjoint nonempty blocks;
dividing by $k!$ forgets the order.  Thus $g^k/k!$ counts unordered partitions
into $k$ decorated blocks.  If every object has a unique set of connected
components and weights multiply across components, then

$$\text{all objects}=\exp(\text{connected objects}),\qquad
\text{connected objects}=\log(\text{all objects}).$$

For example, if $A[S]$ counts all allowed structures on $S$ and $C[S]$ counts
the connected ones, first compute $C=\log A$ and then read $C[U]$ for the
desired vertex set $U$.  The factorials must be invertible; in small
characteristic use a division-free formulation or explicit partition
coefficients.

Dedicated Newton/differential recurrences compute polynomial composition, exp,
and related operations in $\Theta(n^2 2^n)$, rather than repeating subset
convolution for every power.  Their preconditions mirror ordinary formal power
series: $\exp(g)$ needs $g[\varnothing]=0$, and $\log(f)$ needs
$f[\varnothing]=1$.

## 3. Recognition patterns

- A value is attached to every labelled subset and a transition partitions it: subset convolution.
- Count arbitrary objects from connected ones: set-series exponential.
- Recover connected objects from arbitrary ones: set-series logarithm.
- Need all numbers of components: compose an EGF with a set series.
- Need $\sum_S w[S][x^{S}]g^{k}$ for every $k$: power projection, the transpose of composition.

The modelling question comes before the transform: ask whether a label may be
used by both subobjects.  If yes, this is not subset convolution; it may be OR
convolution or an ordinary product instead.

## 4. Pitfalls

- $x^{S}$ denotes a square-free monomial, not an ordinary integer exponent.
- OR convolution permits overlap; subset convolution does not.
- Rank layers above `popcount(mask)` are garbage and must be cleared.
- $\exp$ needs zero constant term in its argument; $\log$ needs constant term one.
- Constants are large: test up to $n=5$ against explicit enumeration of set partitions.
